sections.h2: What does the Alamance County Register of Deeds do for a home seller?
sections.html:
The office records the deed that moves title from you to the buyer, and it keeps the public record of every deed, deed of trust, plat and easement in the county. It acts as a recording office only. The office states that North Carolina law bars its staff from practicing law, so it cannot supply legal forms or explain what a document means for you.

Graham is the county seat and Burlington is the largest community. A house in Burlington, Graham, Mebane, Elon or Haw River is recorded in the same office, and the county is divided into thirteen townships.

Hours differ by service. The office is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., but documents must be presented for recording by 4:30 p.m. under G.S. 153A-94(b). Recording help is available by phone through the office's menu, and a separate menu option handles earlier recorded documents.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees at the Alamance County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
A standard deed costs $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each page after that. A deed of trust or mortgage costs $64 for the first 35 pages and $4 per added page. The county's published schedule is below.

Recording and copy fees listed by the Alamance County Register of Deeds
ItemFee
Deed$26 for pages 1 to 15, then $4 per page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64 for pages 1 to 35, then $4 per page
Multiple documents in one filing$10 added to the recording fee
Non-standard document$25 added to the recording fee
Plat$21
Certified copy$5 for the first page, $2 per added page
Uncertified copy$0.25 per page

Vital record fees on the same schedule, such as marriage licenses and certified birth, death and marriage certificates, are cash or money order only. Ask the office which payment types it accepts for recording before you go.

sections.h2: How much is the North Carolina excise tax on a deed?
sections.html:
The rate is $1.00 for each $500 of the price or value conveyed, with any fraction of $500 counted as a full unit. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the duty on the transferor, who must pay the register of deeds in the county where the land lies before the instrument is recorded. If a parcel spans several counties, the tax goes to the county holding the greater part of the value.

The register of deeds passes the money to the county finance officer. Half stays in the county's general fund, and the other half goes to the state Department of Revenue, less refunds and the county's allowance for administrative costs. The statute also reaches timber deeds and contracts for standing timber.

The county's fee schedule does not list the excise tax, because it is a tax and not a recording fee. Your closing attorney figures it from the consideration stated in the deed and collects it with the recording fee. Ask for the number on your settlement statement before closing day instead of estimating it on your own.

sections.h2: What formatting rules must a deed meet in Alamance County?
sections.html:
A paper deed must follow the standards in G.S. 161-14(b), and the county repeats them on its recording page. A document that fails them can still be recorded, but the office adds a $25 non-standard document fee.

  • Paper size of 8.5 by 11 inches or 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • A blank margin of three inches at the top of the first page, and at least a half inch on the other sides of the first page and on every side of later pages.
  • Black type or print on white paper in a legible font. Nine point is the statutory floor, and blanks or corrections may be made in pen.
  • Text on one side of each page only.
  • The type of instrument stated at the top of the first page, below the margin.

Plats are held to a physical standard of their own. The county accepts only mylar plats in an 18 by 24 inch size. Include a self-addressed stamped envelope of the right size so the recorded document comes back to you.

sections.h2: What happens to the deed after it is recorded?
sections.html:
The register of deeds endorses the day and hour of presentation on the instrument and records instruments in the exact order they arrive. State law requires the document to be indexed and cross-indexed no later than 30 days after presentation. The county issues a book and page number, which is the reference you will use for any later question.

Before recording, every deed except timber deeds and releases goes to the county Tax Department for delinquent tax certification. Unpaid county tax on the parcel will stop the process until it is cleared, which makes a payoff request part of any closing in Alamance County.

The county's e-recording option accepts all documents except plats, so a settlement attorney can submit a deed electronically through an approved vendor. Once recorded, the Tax Department's Land Records staff update the owner name and mailing address. A simple sale shows up faster than a split or subdivision, and an owner who sees nothing after several weeks should call with the book and page number.

sections.h2: How do I search or copy Alamance County land records?
sections.html:
Use the Register of Deeds online search to look up recorded deeds by name, and visit the office for certified copies. The website reminds users that online records are unofficial, so the official record is the one held at the office.

  • A certified copy costs $5 for the first page and $2 for each additional page.
  • An uncertified copy costs $0.25 per page.
  • Parcel ownership, mailing address and legal description appear in the Tax Department's property record search.
  • Tax maps are kept for assessment and are not surveys, so use a licensed surveyor and the recorded plat to settle a boundary.

For a mortgage you are paying off, ask the lender to record the release. Cancellation of a deed of trust is a recorded instrument too.

sections.h2: What local facts affect a deed transfer in Alamance County?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau lists 83,187 housing units for July 2025 and 70,062 households for 2020 to 2024, with 2.44 people per household. About 89.3% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and 28.7% of adults 25 and older held a bachelor's degree or higher. The 2025 population estimate of 186,177 is up 8.6% from the April 2020 base, so the office handles a steady flow of conveyances.

The county was formed in 1849 from Orange County, and the Battle of Alamance in May 1771 gave the area its name. If the title for your house runs through an estate, the Clerk of Superior Court files the estate documents and the register of deeds records what the court or the heirs sign.

faqs.q: What time must a deed be submitted for recording in Alamance County?
faqs.a: By 4:30 p.m. on a business day. The office stays open until 5:00 p.m., but the cut-off for recording documents comes earlier under G.S. 153A-94(b).

faqs.q: Who pays the North Carolina excise tax on a deed?
faqs.a: The transferor pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. The rate in G.S. 105-228.30 is $1.00 per $500 of consideration or value, counting any fraction of $500.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Alamance County?
faqs.a: The recording fee is $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for each added page. A $25 non-standard fee applies if the document breaks the formatting rules.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed electronically in Alamance County?
faqs.a: Yes. The office accepts e-recording of all documents except plats through approved vendors. Your settlement attorney usually handles the submission.

faqs.q: Why did my deed have to go to the Tax Department first?
faqs.a: Deeds recorded after May 2, 2011, other than timber deeds and releases, need delinquent tax certification from the county Tax Department before recording. Unpaid county tax must be cleared first.
